status: Introduction for first-time viewers. The retained workflow supplies the scan, conversation, patch report, and actual pull request. Gateways and agent locations are shown separately.

scenes.text: Orka runs AI agents and coordinates their work across teams, with permissions you control. It's open source.
A web app needs a security review. Security agents find vulnerabilities. You request the fix in Teams, and an engineering agent prepares it.
Orka starts the scheduled scan. The agents find undiscovered security vulnerabilities in source code.
Here, an image URL can become a server command. The security agents trace the input through the code and record the evidence.
In Microsoft Teams, you ask what needs attention. Orka Bot explains the finding. You decide whether to request a fix.
You request the fix. A custom demo integration sends the finding to Engineering, using that team's permissions.
The engineering agent prepares the patch and reports three passing focused tests. Orka publishes separately, keeping Git credentials outside the coding agent.
The result is a pull request, a proposed code change. You can inspect the patch and test report before deciding whether to merge it.
Track reported token usage for each task.

Send requests through Microsoft Teams, Microsoft Scout, Telegram, Slack, or your own gateway. Run native agents in Kubernetes, optionally with Agent Sandbox and Agent Substrate. Connect agents on your laptop, for example in Docker, Foundry hosted agents, or your own compatible agent.
A vulnerability found. A fix tested. A pull request ready for human review. Explore Orka and build workflows for your team.
